question.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $\boldsymbol{f}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ is defined by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/286bec34ba72c733264e8223150d56566d0f61797cb221bed0af0323c3e190c9.svg) 

where $f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_m$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $\boldsymbol f$ is differentiable at $\mathbf{x},$ then the total derivative of $\boldsymbol f$ at $\mathbf{x},$ denoted $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf{x}),$ is given by the $m \times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/33b42ebfc6c3f32ef92212f61a138080543e2e2981088f7b5760b23f7ac31c6c.svg)

In our case, we have the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/354f034a96ffe5bde885644792f50636dc8cbde6f00d65159b0bdefdd836fa09.svg)

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y)=2xy, & \,\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y)={x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/900488a105afb5aa10e9113db36cd9f2e834eac46300d7c0a521a7100ae0d88f.svg)

and $\boldsymbol{f}'$ at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/ed7c974c8fca89e98f542231572e558caf867b200843d2b222ccda4c68a1c33b.svg) is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14196264/assets/abd152888f711ecd43a47e31269e40985178782591546e9d96912fd4c230afa0.svg)
